answer: Beacons in different regions send unpredictable signal challenges; each identity must reply within tight latency bounds consistent with a single physical location, like a comet timed from separate observatories. One honest agent answers from its real position. A sybil farmer running a thousand fakes from one canyon of servers produces identical timing signatures, so the cluster counts as one identity. To pass, each fake needs a distinct machine in a distinct place, turning cheap keys into real hosting costs.
